method: One row per tested hypothesis; statistics and p-values read from the named artifact fields (or computed from them by the formula in `test`). Status uses the p-value as the test was run: supported below alpha 0.05, inconclusive from 0.05 to 0.10, not_supported at 0.10 or above or when the estimate points the wrong way (a failure to reject, not evidence against the hypothesis; underpowered marks a test whose recorded power is below its target). Benjamini-Hochberg q-values and Holm adjusted p-values are computed across the rows with a p-value, on p_two_sided (the directional one-sided p doubled, capped at 1), leaving out rows selected_after_search (a model picked as the best of a field on the same sample; their adjusted fields are null and their note names the search-adjusted test where one exists or says none does) and rows whose test the artifact could not compute. t_equivalent = normal quantile of p_two_sided; clears_hlz_t3 applies the Harvey-Liu-Zhu (2016) t > 3 hurdle.

rows.hypothesis: Walk-forward without the purge, a 1-nearest-neighbour model on block-shuffled CL=F returns (20-session blocks permuted, so structure longer than a block is destroyed and little or no signal is expected) beats its base rate, the accuracy of always calling the more frequent direction, in every run.
rows.test: one-sided exact binomial test of each run's accuracy against that run's base rate; p is the largest of the per-run p-values (intersection-union test, valid however the runs depend on one another)
rows.note: Predicted analytically before the simulation: 1/2 + arcsin(0.8)/pi = 79.5% for the newest leaked label. The shuffled runs permute the same CL=F returns, so they are not independent samples and a test pooled over them (pooled_binomial_p_value_vs_50) would overstate the evidence; real 5-session returns rise more often than they fall, so each run's no-skill accuracy is its base rate, not 50%. The p-value is therefore the largest of the runs' own binomial p-values against their base rates. This test replaced the pooled one after the runs were seen, so the row is not marked pre-specified.

rows.hypothesis: The QLIKE difference between the model of record and Persistence (RV5) moves with what is known at the decision: its last matured value, OVX and the OVX/RV5 gap.
rows.test: Giacomini-White (2006), conditional part: the QLIKE difference on its value 5 sessions earlier, ln OVX of the session before and ln(OVX/RV5), around their means; uncentred HAC, truncated kernel at 4 lags (the 5-session overlap); chi-squared with 3 df; two-sided. The theory assumes forecasts re-estimated on rolling windows of bounded size, which is also what lets it compare nested models; the lab's windows expand and HAR-RV and the OVX-only regression are nested in HAR-IV, so the p-value is approximate.
rows.note: The instruments, the kernel and its lags were fixed after prototype runs on this sample (docs/METHODOLOGY.md section 7). The test with the constant (context p_with_constant) mostly repeats the full-sample DM test, so the ledger registers the conditional part.

rows.hypothesis: Given what was known at each decision, the model of record and Persistence (RV5) were not equally accurate in expectation at every date: in some window of the out-of-sample days their expected QLIKE difference is not zero.
rows.test: Giacomini-Rossi (2010) fluctuation test as a rolling Diebold-Mariano t over windows of 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4 and 0.5 of the out-of-sample days, each standardized by its own long-run variance (truncated kernel, 4 lags: under the null the only autocorrelation is the 5-session overlap); sup |t| for each window length against the test's limit, simulated with a fixed seed at this sample's length; the p-value is the smallest of the five, adjusted for the choice on the same simulation; two-sided. The theory assumes forecasts re-estimated on rolling windows of bounded size, which is also what lets it compare nested models; the lab's windows expand and HAR-RV and the OVX-only regression are nested in HAR-IV, so the p-value is approximate.
rows.note: The window lengths (mu = 0.1-0.5), the per-window variance and the simulated critical values were fixed after prototype runs on this sample; the p-value adjusts for the choice among the five window lengths, and the seed was fixed before the production build. The null includes equal average loss, so where the full-sample DM test rejects (context dm_p) the row mostly repeats it. Each window is scaled by its own variability, so the window of the largest |t| is where the difference was most consistent, not where it was largest. The mu = 0.1 p in context is anti-conservative under the null (docs/METHODOLOGY.md section 7).
